meta._: ---- the rest is documentation, not settings ----
whyYouTube: Instagram's embed has no JavaScript API at all: it cannot autoplay, cannot seek, never says when a clip ends, and its own end-card play button is a link to instagram.com that has to be blocked.
It also throttles a browser that opens many embeds, and a throttled frame is indistinguishable from a deleted post - which is what made the on-screen count drift.
YouTube's iframe API gives all of it properly: autoplay, a real scrub bar, a true 'ended' event, and an explicit error code when a video is gone or not embeddable.
The one cost is advertising. Family Guy is Content-ID claimed by Fox, so some of these may serve a pre-roll. tools/ad-check.py measures it per video rather than guessing.
howToEdit: The clip list lives in links.txt - one URL per line. Add a line, delete a line. That is the whole job.
Order matters: the list is kept best-first (most watched first), so the top of the file is the strongest material.
A line starting with # is ignored, so you can park a link without losing it.
Numbering is automatic and no title is needed; an untitled clip shows as "?" on the reel, which keeps the surprise.
Any link type still works if you want to mix: YouTube, Shorts, Vimeo, Instagram, a direct .mp4, or videos/file.mp4 in this repo.
